Lesson · 20 min

Present, Share, and Download

Skip slides you're not ready to show, present with presenter view or in Google Meet, share the presentation at the right access level, and download PowerPoint and PDF copies.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Skip a slide so it doesn't appear in the slideshow
  • ✓Present from the beginning and use presenter view with speaker notes
  • ✓Present Google Slides in a Google Meet call
  • ✓Share a presentation as Viewer, Commenter, or Editor, and download it as a PowerPoint or PDF file

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Ready for orientation

On the job

The welcome presentation is almost done.

A draft slide about parking isn't approved yet. Denise will present at orientation, sometimes over Google Meet for tenants who can't come in. Andre Wallace, the leasing agent, wants to suggest changes. The lobby screen needs a PowerPoint copy, and new tenants get a PDF by email.

Your task: Hide the draft slide, rehearse, share with Andre, and make both downloads.

  • To skip a slide, right-click it in the filmstrip and choose Skip slide. It stays in the file but doesn't appear in the slideshow. Choose it again to show the slide.
  • Skipping is safer than deleting a slide you'll need later: the content and its notes stay in the presentation.

Present your slides

  • Slideshow (top right) presents full screen from the slide you're on. The arrow next to Slideshow has Present from beginning and Presenter view.
  • Presenter view opens a separate window with your speaker notes, a timer, and the next slide, while the audience sees only the slides. It works best with a second screen or projector.
  • Move through the slides with the arrow keys. Home goes to the first slide and End to the last; type a slide number and press Enter to jump to it.
  • While presenting, press S to open speaker notes, L for the laser pointer, and B or W for a blank black or white screen (press any key to return).
  • Press Esc to stop presenting.
Present in Google Meet (work or school accounts, in Chrome): in the Meet call, select Present now › A tab, choose the presentation's tab, and select Share. Then select Start slideshow in Meet. You can show your speaker notes and add a co-presenter. In PowerPoint and Teams, the matching step is sharing PowerPoint Live in the Teams meeting.

Share or download?

Share the Google Slides file when people should see the current version and work with you. Download a copy when someone needs a separate file: a PowerPoint for a screen that runs PowerPoint, or a PDF for people who only need to read it. A downloaded copy doesn't update when you change the original.

  • Share: select Share (top right), type the person's name or email, choose Viewer, Commenter, or Editor, and select Send.
  • PowerPoint copy: File › Download › Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx).
  • PDF copy: File › Download › PDF Document (.pdf).

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Finish your practice presentation in your own Google Account.

  1. Skip one slide. Then start the slideshow from the beginning and check that it doesn't appear.
  2. Open presenter view and practice with your speaker notes.
  3. Share the presentation with a classmate (or a second account of your own) as a Commenter.
  4. Download it as a PDF and as a PowerPoint (.pptx) file. Open the PDF to check it.
Deliverable: Submit the PDF of your presentation and a screenshot of the Share box showing the Commenter to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Google Slides, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
